answer: An agent economy can require every identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it can submit work, then slash that stake when randomly sampled audits reveal fabricated outputs. The atlas registry links each stake to one active identity, while falcon auditors compare claims against independent evidence through a prism of rotating checks. Creating thousands of accounts no longer creates free influence: the attacker must immobilize capital for each one and risks losing it with every detected lie.
